label: 50% — Needs
title: The essentials you can't live without
text: This half of your budget covers the expenses you genuinely can't avoid — the things that keep your life running no matter what. Utility bills, rent or mortgage payments, health care, and groceries all belong here, along with minimum payments on a credit card or loan. If skipping the payment would mean losing housing, going without food, or missing a required bill, it's a need — not a preference.

label: 30% — Wants
title: What you spend on by choice
text: This category covers things you spend money on because they add enjoyment to your life, not because your life depends on them. Streaming subscriptions, hobby supplies, restaurant meals, and vacations are classic examples. For students, this often shows up as eating out with friends, games, non-essential shopping, or entertainment subscriptions — all legitimate spending, just not urgent.

label: 20% — Savings
title: What you set aside for the future
text: The final fifth of your budget is set aside for your future rather than spent right away. This can go toward an emergency fund, retirement contributions, or a savings goal like a down payment, and any extra debt payments beyond the required minimum count here too. For a student, this might look like building a small emergency cushion, saving toward a laptop or a trip, or putting aside part of an allowance each month.
